## My request:
# Role

You are a senior product analyst and documentation engineer. Map chess.com ([https://www.chess.com](https://www.chess.com)) one-to-one from live observation and public sources. Do not invent features.

# Goal

Produce a complete static product package that documents chess.com as it actually works: play, learn, analyze, social, events, membership, and onboarding. Deliverables are HTML only. This is documentation and mock packaging, not a live clone, backend, or released product.

# Scope

Target: [https://www.chess.com](https://www.chess.com) and authenticated public flows you can reach without violating terms.

Must cover:

- Home, Play (Live, Daily, Bots, variants, time controls), Puzzles, Learn/Lessons/Courses, Game Review/Analysis, Insights/Stats, Clubs, Friends, Messages, News/Events/Watch, Membership/pricing, Settings, mobile vs desktop.
- Onboarding: signup/login, first-game path, rating placement if present, first puzzle, first lesson.
- Every visible UI control, empty state, paywall, and error state you can trigger legally.
- Visual system: colors, typography, spacing, board/piece chrome, dark/light if available.

Do not cover private admin, fair-play internals, payment card data, or bypassing paywalls.

# Method

1. Browse the live site systematically. Walk every primary nav item and one level of secondary pages.
2. Interact with each major flow: start a bot game, open a puzzle, open a lesson, open game review if available, open clubs, open membership.
3. Record each feature as: name, location, trigger, behavior, states, free vs premium, screenshot reference.
4. Research only to fill gaps you cannot observe (feature names, membership matrix). Cite sources.
5. If a step is blocked (login wall, missing file, tool unavailable), log the blocker and continue. Do not fake completion.

# Output (HTML only, chess.com visual language)

Produce separate HTML files that reuse chess.com’s green/dark board aesthetic, fonts, and layout rhythm:

1. BRD
2. PRFAQ
3. PRD
4. SPEC
5. Traceability matrix (requirement → screen → evidence screenshot)
6. CEO review
7. Engineer review
8. QA review + test plan
9. Mockups, each linked to its source screenshot
10. Reference board: screenshot vs mock side-by-side
11. Prototype QA report: six primary routes, responsive + keyboard checks, console-error log
12. Independent validation summary with explicit PASS / FAIL / PARKED counts

# Quality bar

- One-to-one mapping: every documented control must exist on the live site or be marked PARKED with reason.
- No filler. No plugin-loading theater. No unused skill names.
- If evidence is missing, PARK it. Do not mark PASS.
- Static package only.

# Stop conditions

Done when all listed HTML artifacts exist, every mapped feature has evidence or a PARKED note, and blockers are listed in the validation summary.

- reproduce documented workflows and interaction concepts;
- use original or properly licensed artwork and branding;
